Payment reminder email for plumbers

Plumbers bill in several ways: on the spot, to property managers, through warranty companies and in stages. Here is a plan for each, with wording to copy.

Checked 2026-11-21. Menus in other products change, so a label may differ slightly on your screen.

Short answer: match the reminder to how the job was billed. A call-out paid on the day needs a prompt the next morning. A property manager needs the right invoice or PO number and a nudge before their pay run. A large repipe needs a reminder for each milestone, not just the last one. Below is a schedule and four emails and one text you can copy.

How plumbing jobs get billed, and why it changes the reminder

A plumber does not have one kind of customer. Four kinds of job need four different habits.

  • Emergency call-outs. A burst pipe at 9 p.m. is meant to be paid on the day. Many companies send the invoice from the truck as soon as the work is done, so the customer can review and pay while the job is fresh. If it was not paid, the customer is often still stressed or never saw the email, so the first nudge should be quick and kind.
  • Property managers and landlords. They often pay on their own cycle and may need a work order number, a unit number or approval from the owner before the invoice can be paid. A late invoice here is often an incomplete invoice.
  • Insurance and home-warranty jobs. Someone else pays all or part. Warranty companies commonly require approval before the work, and the homeowner may owe a service fee. The contract varies by company, so check the one you work with. Chase the right person: the warranty company for its share and the homeowner for theirs.
  • Repipes and remodels. Larger jobs are usually billed in stages, such as a deposit, rough-in and final completion. State each payment amount and due date in the agreement before work starts. Each stage is its own invoice that can go late.

A reminder schedule for plumbers

  1. Day-of call-outs: send the invoice when the job ends. If it is still open the next morning, send a short nudge. If it is open after a week, send the overdue email.
  2. Net 30 accounts (property managers, commercial): a friendly note three to five days before the due date, one on the due date, an overdue note about a week after, a firmer one at two weeks, and a final notice near 30 days late.
  3. Warranty and insurance jobs: check the claim status first. Remind the customer only for their own share, such as a service fee or a denied part, and contact the warranty company for the rest.
  4. Deposits and progress payments: remind on the milestone due date, not after the whole job. A late deposit is the one to chase hardest, because materials are already bought. Do not start the next stage until the last one is settled, if your agreement says so.

For more on timing, see how often to send invoice reminders. For the general method, see how to chase overdue invoices by email.

1. Friendly, before or on the due date

Best for property managers and progress payments. Put the address in the subject line, since a manager may have fifty properties.

Subject: Invoice [invoice number] for [job address], due [due date] Hi [name], Thanks again for having us out to [job address]. A reminder that invoice [invoice number] for [amount] is due on [due date]. The invoice is attached. You can pay here: [pay link] If you've already sent it, thank you, and please ignore this note. If something on the invoice doesn't look right, reply and I'll sort it out. [your name] [business name], [phone]

2. Overdue

This one asks for a payment date and offers to fix what is blocking it. It suits a missing PO or an owner approval.

Subject: Invoice [invoice number] for [job address] is past due Hi [name], Our records show invoice [invoice number] for [amount] was due on [due date] and is still open. A copy is attached. If it has already gone out, could you send me the date or check number so I can match it? If it hasn't, you can pay here: [pay link] If it is waiting on an approval or a purchase order number on your side, tell me what you need from us and I'll send it today. [your name] [business name], [phone]

3. Firmer

Only name a consequence you would carry out. Late fees and their amounts depend on your customer agreement and state law.

Subject: Invoice [invoice number] is [days] days overdue Hi [name], Invoice [invoice number] for [amount], for the work at [job address], was due on [due date]. I have not had payment or a reply to my earlier notes. Please pay by [new date], or call me on [phone] today if there is a problem with the invoice or you need to set up a payment plan. Pay here: [pay link] If we can't settle this by [new date], we will have to [hold future non-emergency scheduling for the account / apply the late fee in our service terms]. I would much rather sort it out with you directly. [your name] [business name]

4. Final notice

Lien rights on larger jobs come with deadlines that differ by state, so check yours early. This is not legal advice.

Subject: Final notice: invoice [invoice number] Hi [name], This is my final written reminder about invoice [invoice number] for [amount] for the work at [job address]. It was due on [due date] and is now [days] days overdue. Payment is needed by [final date]. After that date we will [step you will actually take, such as sending the account to collections or ending the account]. Pay here: [pay link], or call me on [phone] if you want to talk it through first. [your name] [business name]

A short text for a call-out

A text works well for a homeowner who paid nothing on the day. Send it only if the customer agreed to texts, for example on the work order, and stop if they reply STOP. A person who agreed to a visit has not necessarily agreed to texts.

Hi [name], this is [business name]. Invoice [invoice number] for [amount] from the work at [job address] was due [due date]. You can pay here: [pay link]. Questions? Call [phone]. Reply STOP to stop texts.

Check these four things before you send

  • Is it paid? A check or card payment from this morning may not be posted yet.
  • Is a third party involved? If a warranty company or insurer owes part of it, chase the right one.
  • Does the invoice carry what the payer needs? Property managers often need the work order number, unit and owner name on it.
  • Is there a callback or a dispute? If the customer is unhappy with the repair, fix that first. A reminder will only make it worse.

What your software can and cannot do

Most invoicing tools can send a reminder when an invoice is past due. They usually send the same wording to everyone. They do not know that a customer is a warranty company, that a property manager is waiting on an owner, or that a deposit matters more than a final bill. Read the open list yourself each week, set aside the accounts that need a call, and send reminders to the rest. In QuickBooks Online the automatic reminders are under Settings, then Account and settings, then Sales. The standard reminders cannot leave one customer out, which matters for a warranty company you handle by phone. QuickBooks Online Advanced can, with workflows.
